approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds from score-ranked accepted molecules and recombines a fragment from each of two selected parents. For the first parent it usually keeps the larger side of a random bridge cut, then joins that piece to a donor fragment and may apply a local mutation. A Gaussian process trained on all accepted observations selects a batch from the resulting fresh pool. The random cut can separate ring systems or discard part of a strong first parent's core before the selector sees the product.
approach.novelty: Preserve the first parent's complete ring core during fragment crossover. Choose only pendant cuts whose retained side contains every source ring atom and the paths connecting them, then attach the donor fragment through the existing crossover. This changes the physical fragment retained, whereas earlier siblings changed parent allocation, survival or similarity-based pairing. It also differs from the separate whole-branch pruning experiment: donor replacement and learned pool selection already belong to this Parent, so the new question is whether preserving its core improves recombination.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent's crossover selects an arbitrary non-ring single bond in each parent and favors the larger first-parent fragment with probability 0.80; neither the cut nor its retained orientation protects the complete ring core. A read-only conditional-law audit of all 34,312 logged first-parent crossover attempts finds a ring-bearing source with at least one pendant core-preserving cut in every attempt. Across these exact sources, the inherited first-fragment rule retains all source ring atoms with mean probability 0.581658; 33,404 attempts also offer bridge cuts that separate ring systems. There are 251,851 pendant cut occurrences among 351,534 original bridge-cut occurrences, over 1,972 distinct first-parent identities. These are repeated actual-source opportunities and analytically computed selection probabilities, not reconstructed realized cuts or scored alternative offspring. The Parent evaluates 1,679 crossover offspring, of which 172 beat their best parent, with mean child-minus-best-parent score -0.156871; mutation's corresponding deficit is -0.065053, an observational comparison with different parent references. The prior assortative sibling raised pair similarity but did not improve core reuse or final score, indicating that related parents alone do not ensure intact useful structures survive the unchanged crossover. The molecular assessment also reports fragmented cores and large repeated assemblies. A different lineage's ring-preserving whole-branch deletion reached evaluation but usually lost score and regrew, so preservation must be tested within useful recombination rather than assumed beneficial from compactness alone.
hypothesis: When forming a crossover's first-parent fragment, sample only pendant single-bond cuts and retain the side containing every source ring atom and its connecting linkers.

finding_summary.headline: First-parent ring cores survived crossover, but final scores fell on all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: Physical inheritance of the first parent’s complete ring system worked and reached evaluation, but the full-core restriction did not improve the complete method. The crossover cohort produced more parent-beating descendants while the complete search ended at lower scores, so that local diagnostic is insufficient to establish improved optimization. It rules out failed cutting or lack of exposure to the selector as the explanation for the negative utility result. Keeping every ring can also keep a large or unproductive framework, while the donor adds more structure and useful peripheral functional relationships can still be removed. Optional mutation can then undo the protected structure. The supplied chemistry is consistent with this limit: conventional arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with duplicated frameworks, dense bridges, reactive substituents and unspecified stereochemistry. The next useful distinction is which core and attachment relationships deserve preservation, and when replacement or simplification is beneficial; this result does not establish that all rings should always survive. The observed crossover subgroups differ in parents and later edits, and the changed random-call schedule alters subsequent search history. Neither the subgroup score difference nor molecular size identifies an individual protected cut’s causal value, and unused candidates have no oracle counterfactual labels.
finding_summary.results: Across 34,564 informative first-parent fragment calls, the inherited rule would retain the complete source ring/linker core with mean probability 55.968%; the applied pendant-cut rule made that probability one. All 33,626 sanitized protected crossovers preserved the original core atoms and bonds before canonicalization. Protected crossovers reached 28,875 novel pool descendants and 1,714 actual evaluated descendants; 1,587 of those emissions followed an immediate crossover that changed the first parent’s identity. Of 600 evaluated crossover descendants with a later mutation, 224 no longer contained the original typed ring/linker core. One additional unselected immediate-only pool product changed aromatic representation during the inherited canonicalization step. Mean emitted size rose from 33.39 to 40.90 heavy atoms, and 938 attempted products exceeded the unchanged 120-atom limit. The protected crossover cohort had 210/1,714 strict best-parent beats and mean child-minus-best-parent score -0.112347, compared with 172/1,679 and -0.156871 in the Parent’s crossover cohort. All fifteen Child task/seed runs completed. Mean final score fell from 0.544374 to 0.529067, a paired change of -0.015307; all three paired seeds declined (-0.014873, -0.022309, -0.008738). The mean DRD2 change was -0.090254, despite gains on three other tasks.

molecular.headline: Compact arylamide and sulfinamide leaders coexist with repeated large frameworks, dense bridges, and reactive substituents
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied current and parent trajectory was read; all tasks and seeds are covered. Each current task contains 900 observations and 870 optimizer proposals. The current proposals are consistently substantial molecules: ring-closure and branch presence are 1.0 throughout, and aromatic-token presence ranges from 0.9931 to 1.0. These text counters indicate whether a SMILES contains the relevant token, not aromatic atom fractions or feasible three-dimensional rings. Small fragments are not the visible limiting chemistry. Instead, the low-scoring excerpts repeatedly join complete arylamide or dione systems, and one population has mean SMILES length 130.8. More compact leaders include ordinary N-methyl arylamides and a recognizable tertiary-amine/cyclobutane/sulfinamide series. Other families use densely bridged nitrogen/carbonyl rings or N-fluorinated enol/thiol-containing structures. Drug-like functional groups are therefore present, but synthetic plausibility and stability are uneven. Explicit tetrahedral stereolabel rates are zero throughout; formal charge tokens are rare, appearing at rate 0.0034 in the arylamide population and zero elsewhere. Neutral drawings can still contain basic amines. Several seed families provide moderate structural diversity, while much nominal variety comes from decoration, repeated units, or additional bridges. Relative to the parent, some leading chemistry becomes more conventional, but size, topology, and reactive bond liabilities remain.

per_task.generated_character: The best current family consists of compact fused/bridged heteroaromatics carrying an ordinary N-methyl phenylamide, methoxy or methylamino substitution, small alkyl groups, and a carbon-bound fluorine on a ring bridge. Nearby leaders replace phenyl with pyridyl or use sulfur/nitrogen ring connections. The leading molecule avoids the direct amide N-F bond seen in the parent's seed-2 leader, although other current seeds still produce N-fluorinated or N-chlorinated heteroaromatic amides. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9989, and mean SMILES length 47.2. The compact leading architecture and standard amide are recognizable, but ring-bridge geometry and stereochemical identity still require assessment. The low excerpt instead contains duplicated, often heavily decorated arylamide systems connected through N/O/S or carbon linkages.
liabilities: Fluorinated bridge connectivity and dense fusion make accessible geometry and stereoisomer identity uncertain.
Bromomethyl and chloromethoxy variants add potential reactivity without establishing a general score advantage.
Other seed families retain direct N-F/N-Cl or additional N-N connections.
Joining complete arylamide systems sharply enlarges the molecules and appears repeatedly among the lowest supplied scores.
missing_features: Matched simpler bridge connections retaining the leading N-methyl arylamide and substituent relationships are insufficiently represented.
The substituted fluorinated bridge has no explicit stereochemical identity.
Stable compact alternatives are still incompletely represented across seeds, where direct N-halogen bonds and duplicated arylamides remain.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methoxy/methyl/fluorinated-bridge N-methyl phenylamide reaches 0.459794. Replacing phenyl with pyridyl lowers the score to 0.442564; replacing the aryl methyl with fluoromethyl gives 0.441920. In that fluoromethyl series, replacing methoxy with methylamino gives 0.458807, and fluoromethyl-to-bromomethyl exchange ties at 0.458807. Extending methylamino to ethylamino then lowers a closely related final structure to 0.299139. These local changes reveal specific substituent preferences, not a general benefit from adding fluorine, nitrogen, or size. Repeated arylamide assemblies score as low as 3.62e-22 despite retaining the apparent core functionality. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds the parent's 0.416350 while replacing an N-fluoroamide with N-methyl amide chemistry and a different bridged core. The parent's overall maximum was 0.446352 in another bridged N/O-carbonyl family. This is evidence of a different productive molecular arrangement, not proof that any individual bridge or fluorine position is required.

per_task.generated_character: This population is dominated by large, extensively linked aromatic structures. The leading family contains a benzopyranone-like carbonyl core, biaryl connections, a terminal ethynyl group, and repeated pyridyl/diazine-type rings linked through ethers. Carbon-bound fluorine, chlorine, methyl, and methoxy substituents decorate the extended framework. Its ring sizes and bond types are more recognizable than the unusual heteroatom-halogen chemistry in some parent leaders, but the overall assembly is very large and rich in aromatic acceptors with little donor functionality. Other seeds make still larger mixtures of repeated carbonyl heterocycles, imine/enol-ether connections, and unsaturated chains. Mean SMILES length is 130.8 and maximum 232, with aromatic and ring presence both 1.0. Synthetic assembly and physical properties are major unresolved issues even where individual substructures are ordinary.
liabilities: The large aromatic surface and many connecting bonds create unresolved solubility, permeability, and synthesis concerns; none is measured here.
Repeated azaaryl-ether units add considerable molecular size without a monotonic supplied-score gain.
Some neighboring molecules introduce ethynyl ethers, imines, cumulated bonds, thiocarbonyls, or other labile unsaturated connections.
Extensive late ring closure and appendage growth increase synthetic complexity while remaining near the same score region.
missing_features: More compact frameworks retaining the useful heteroaryl and carbonyl relationships are underrepresented.
Matched removal of remote repeated rings is only partially demonstrated, despite the favorable methoxy simplification.
Balanced polar functionality and fewer aromatic connections are not established within the leading high-acceptor, low-donor series.
Stable short alternatives to the imine/enol-ether appendages remain insufficiently represented.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The terminal-methoxy version of the extended heteroaryl-ether framework scores 0.611490. Replacing that small group with an additional heteroaryloxy appendage gives 0.608641; much longer unsaturated appendages score 0.608404-0.610960. The smaller peripheral arrangement therefore does at least as well within the supplied family. Several different changes tie at 0.608641, including chlorine/methyl exchange on a remote ring, ether-to-thioether substitution, and carbonyl-to-thiocarbonyl substitution in related molecules. These ties provide no evidence that extra remote size or sulfur is needed. Low optimizer molecules already contain substantial aryl/carbonyl frameworks at 0.523237-0.527966, showing that rings and heteroatoms alone are insufficient. The current maximum is slightly above the parent's seed-2 value of 0.608345 but below the parent's overall 0.632470. Its leading chemistry replaces the parent's linked N-halogenated diones with long heteroaryl ethers; other current seed maxima are lower than their parent counterparts and remain very large.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family is chemically recognizable: an N-propyl tertiary amine connects a substituted cyclobutane/anisyl group to a branched chain bearing an aryl sulfinamide. The sulfinamide contains a single S=O group, and the other aromatic ring is a chlorinated pyridine. Related molecules exchange carbon-bound halogens, fluorinate alkyl groups, or modify methoxy/thioether substitution. These structures contain a potentially basic tertiary amine, a sulfinamide NH, an oxidized sulfur acceptor, and hydrophobic aromatic groups. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9977, halogen presence 1.0, and mean SMILES length 75.6. The ordinary sulfinamide and cyclobutane are not inherently evidence of implausible chemistry, but several carbon and sulfur stereochemical distinctions are unspecified. Other seeds produce more bridged aryl amines or larger amide-linked cages, including unusual combined S=N/S=S sulfur functionality.
liabilities: The leading sulfinamide and substituted saturated carbons can generate stereoisomers with different geometry, but no configuration is specified.
Chloromethyl and extended halogenated alkyl variants introduce additional reactivity or size concerns.
Some late cages combine imino and thiocarbonyl bonding at sulfur with difficult polycyclic topology.
Large amide-linked cage assemblies retain considerable hydrophobic surface and connecting-group complexity at lower supplied scores.
missing_features: Stereochemically defined sulfinamide sulfur, branched carbon, and substituted cyclobutane arrangements are absent.
Matched simpler side-chain and aryl substitution alternatives preserving the useful tertiary-amine relationship are incompletely represented.
More ordinary connections are missing within the lower-scoring, highly bridged sulfur-cage branch.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The dichloropyridyl sulfinamide/tertiary-amine leader scores 0.981641; exchanging one pyridyl chlorine for fluorine gives exactly the same score. Replacing the branched ethyl portion with fluoromethyl gives 0.972794, while longer halogenated alkoxy decorations reach 0.963293. These observations favor the complete aryl/amine/sulfinamide arrangement and show no universal advantage from additional fluorination or peripheral growth. Low molecules include an aryl acid/amide/N-sulfonyl cyclic-amine assembly at 0.007264 and a protected polyol-rich amine-containing structure at 0.011436. Nitrogen or ring presence alone is therefore insufficient. The current seed-0 maximum is below the parent's 0.990833 spiro-amine maximum, while changing to a more open sulfinamide/cyclobutane series. Current seed-1 reaches 0.962141 in another aryl-amine family, but seed-2 peaks at 0.718928 in a much more complex amide-linked sulfur cage. The high-scoring ordinary sulfinamide series demonstrates that exotic sulfur bonding is not universally needed.

per_task.generated_character: The strongest family consists of densely bridged polycycles carrying alkyl/ethoxy-substituted aromatic rings, partly saturated nitrogen rings, and an N-methyl carbonyl-rich ring. The leader contains an N-N connection within the carbonyl-containing ring closure; nearby analogues replace that connection with carbon or alter bridge length and saturation. Other seed families include large fused aromatic diones and linked aryl/N-methyl lactams, some with tightly oxygen-bridged azaaromatic fragments. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9977, and mean SMILES length 61.8. Halogen presence is only 0.0989. The functional groups provide recognizable carbonyl and aromatic chemistry, but the crowded bridge network is synthetically demanding and its conformations are unspecified.
liabilities: Overlapping bridges and unsaturated ring connections make synthesis and accessible conformation uncertain.
The leading N-N connection and related N-O or peroxide structures introduce additional bond-stability questions.
Some linked aryl/lactam molecules contain strongly constrained oxygen/azaaromatic small-ring closures.
Duplicated carbonyl/aromatic systems substantially increase size while appearing among the lowest supplied scores.
missing_features: Less bridged alternatives retaining the aryl and carbonyl arrangement are insufficiently represented near the leading scores.
Matched removal of the N-N connection and controlled bridge simplification are only partially demonstrated.
Stereochemically specified bridgehead and substituted saturated-ring identities are missing.
Compact alternatives to joining entire aromatic dione or lactam systems remain underrepresented.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-N-containing bridged leader scores 0.231463. Its carbon-connected ring analogue scores 0.225320, while other bridge and saturation variants cluster at 0.221185-0.228396. The modest local differences do not establish that the most complex bridge network is necessary. A different linked aryl/lactam family reaches 0.222716. Low optimizer examples instead duplicate or join large aromatic dione systems through ester, anhydride, peroxide, or N/O connections, scoring 0.112181-0.117809. A late doubled structure likewise drops to 0.152283, below simpler final members around 0.21. The current seed-0 maximum is above the parent's 0.224057 expanded nitrogen/carbonyl-ring maximum, while changing to a more extensively bridged cage. The current seed-2 maximum also exceeds its parent's 0.210377, but introduces constrained oxygen-containing ring connections. Neither comparison establishes synthetic ease or resolves the limited score region.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family contains an expanded cyclic dione with direct N-F substitution, fused to a partly unsaturated nitrogen ring bearing pyrrolyl or pyridyl and substituted enol/thiol groups. The best attaches a fluoromethyl/fluorine-substituted cyclobutenol carrying a vinylic thiol; a near-leader instead uses a fluoropyridyl group and a larger cyclopentenol/thiol substituent. An open-chain enol/thiol relative is also shown. These are compact carbonyl/heteroaryl molecules, but direct N-fluorination, tautomeric enol/thiol functionality, and strained unsaturated small rings make apparent stability and synthesis questionable. Ring presence is 1.0, aromatic presence 0.9931, and mean SMILES length 58.0. The low excerpt contains large hybrid or repeated dione systems, not a lack of molecular architecture.
liabilities: Direct N-F bonds on the carbonyl-containing ring introduce a distinct reactivity concern.
Cyclobutenol strain and enol/thiol tautomerism complicate stability, synthesis, and interpretation of the drawn structure.
Fluorinated, hydroxylated, and thiolated saturated carbons have unspecified stereochemistry.
Joining complete dione systems yields very large molecules with extremely low supplied scores.
missing_features: Matched ordinary N-substitution alternatives retaining the leading dione and enol/thiol arrangement are missing.
Stable replacements for the tautomeric and potentially reactive thiol/enol region have not been established without changing the rest of the molecule.
Less strained saturated or open-chain connections are only partially represented around the useful heteroaryl/carbonyl relationships.
Explicit stereochemical identities of the fluorinated substituted rings are absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The pyrrolyl/fluorinated-cyclobutenol-thiol leader scores 0.576998; its analogue replacing the saturated ring fluorine with thiol gives 0.555217. The fluoropyridyl/cyclopentenol family reaches 0.571115, versus 0.526837 without that aromatic fluorine and 0.531910 after replacing its saturated ring fluorine with thiol. Within a methyl-substituted cyclobutenol series, replacing the vinylic thiol with hydroxyl causes a particularly large change, from 0.532883 to 0.032767. This is a specific observed functional-group preference, not evidence that all sulfur or fluorine additions help. An open-chain enol/thiol analogue still reaches 0.530545, so a strained small ring is not established as essential. A late doubled molecule scores 1.66e-21, and a large early hybrid scores 2.88e-57. The current seed-2 maximum exceeds its parent's 0.407140 but remains below the parent's overall 0.584558 aryl dione/aminomethyl/fluoromethyl maximum, which had different and more conventional peripheral chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Low-scoring excerpts repeatedly duplicate arylamides or diones, with supplied scores as small as 3.62e-22 and 1.66e-21. One proposal population has mean SMILES length 130.8. Within its leading family, replacing a remote heteroaryloxy appendage with methoxy raises the supplied score from 0.608641 to 0.611490.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator too often joins complete molecular systems instead of preserving a compact productive core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide controlled removal of repeated units and simplification of remote appendages while preserving the informative core and key group relationships. Use accepted local comparisons to determine useful size instead of assuming that retaining two complete parent-like architectures is beneficial.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The cited molecules include fluorinated aromatic bridges, densely overlapping nitrogen/carbonyl cages, constrained oxygen/azaaromatic closures, and unsaturated small rings. Ring-closure presence is already 1.0 throughout, while simpler sulfinamide/cyclobutane chemistry and an open-chain enol/thiol analogue also achieve high local scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Geometric and synthetic feasibility remain unresolved as ring systems acquire additional bridges.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make bridge opening, alternative connection points, ring expansion, and saturation changes accessible while preserving useful functional-group spacing. Treat valence-valid closure as incomplete evidence of accessible geometry or a credible synthesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Several families retain direct N-F or N-Cl bonds, N-N connections, enol/thiol groups, or labile unsaturated appendages. Ordinary N-methyl arylamide and sulfinamide leaders demonstrate access to more conventional bonding. A thiol-to-hydroxyl change can sharply reduce a supplied score, so simple blanket removal of every reactive group would also discard locally useful chemical distinctions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stable functional-group alternatives are not explored systematically around reactive high-scoring structures.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer matched stable substitutions that preserve the surrounding scaffold, polarity pattern, and approximate size, then let current score feedback evaluate them. Distinguish the chemical role of a group from its incidental reactivity instead of copying it uncritically or removing an entire functional class.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest population has zero explicit tetrahedral stereolabel presence. The leading sulfinamide has stereogenic sulfur and substituted carbon connections, while bridged amides and fluorinated enol/thiol rings introduce additional stereochemical distinctions.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity is left unspecified even in families with clear carbon and sulfur stereochemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve stereochemical information through structural changes and make valid local stereoisomers available when new centres arise. Combine this with credible ring geometry and current scoring feedback so that one unspecified connectivity is not treated as a fully defined accessible molecule.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Chlorine/fluorine exchange in a sulfinamide series ties at 0.981641, several remote ether/thioether or carbonyl/thiocarbonyl changes tie at 0.608641, and methylamino-to-ethylamino extension lowers another local score from 0.458807 to 0.299139. Elsewhere, multiple simultaneous ring and connecting-group changes obscure which chemical feature matters.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically local alternatives are too sparse to separate useful functionality from incidental growth and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expand matched changes to substituent position, carbonyl connection, heteroatom identity, amine spacing, and bridge geometry while keeping the remaining structure fixed. Include independently connected, synthetically credible alternatives rather than relying mainly on large rearrangements or repeated units.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
